DIRECTIONS:
In the passages that follow, certain
words and phrases are underlined and numbered. In
the right-hand column, you will find alternatives for the
underlined part. You are to choose the best answer to

choose “
No Change
You will also find questions about a section of the passage,
or about the passage as a whole. These questions do not
refer to an underlined portion of the passage, but rather
are identified by a number or numbers in a box.
For each question, choose the alternative you consider
best and fill in the corresponding oval on your answer
document. Read each passage through once before you
begin to answer the questions that accompany it. For
many of the questions, you must read several sentences
beyond the question to determine the answer. Be sure
that you have read far enough ahead each time you
choose an alternative.

PASSAGE I
A Small Rescue
While surveying a wooded campground near Helena,
Montana, for damaged trees, a team of forestry workers
discovered two baby Western screech owls. Nestled in a
cardboard box lined with blankets and pine boughs, the
birds were delivered to me, a wildlife rehabilitator with
Big Sky Bird Rescue.
The two-week-old owlets were weak and dehydrated
when they arrived at the rescue center. Under my care,
though, the birds enjoyed a steady diet of crickets and
mice, quickly becoming bright-eyed and tripling in weight.
When their flight feathers started coming in, Lila and
Twyla, playfully named by the forestry workers, were
moved from a refuge for very young owls to a spacious
outdoor enclosure.
The writer wants to suggest that an attempt was made to
keep the owls comfortable during transport. Which
choice best accomplishes that goal?
A. No Change
B.
Not making a sound as they huddled together with
their heads tucked in,
C.
Within only an hour or so of being discovered in
the Montana woods,
D.
Seeming not to have been harmed in their fall,
Which transition word or phrase is most logical in
context?
F. No Change
G.
furthermore,
H.
likewise,
J.
after all,
The writer wants to illustrate the contrast in the design
of the two places the owls were housed. Which choice
best accomplishes that goal?
A. No Change
B.
a nest-sized, temperature-controlled container
C.
a safe space in which to reinvigorate and grow
D.
their first home at the rescue
